sentences.text:
eeted for the offence under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act,
1988'), for not holding a valid driving licence and further, there was no permit from the Road Transport Authority to ply the vehicle on the road.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that apart from the Registration Certificate, the Road Transport Authorities also provide Fitness Certificate to the vehicle to ply on the road within the prescribed limits.

In the present case, the limit was prescribed at 60 kms.,
however, the vehicle went beyond the said limit.

3. No proof is filed to show that the driver was convicted for the offence under Section 181 of the Act,
1988.
Mere filing of charge sheet will not disentitle the claimants from claiming compensation on the ground that the driver was not holding a valid licence.
If it is the claim of the Insurance Company that the driver was not holding a valid licence, it is for the Insurance Company to adduce evidence accordingly.

4. Further, it is not the case that there was no permission to the vehicle to ply on the road, however,
the ground is that the vehicle was plied beyond the permissible limit given by the Road Transport Authorities.
This ground also cannot be made basis to refuse compensation.
5. Therefore, both the grounds fail and accordingly, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
However, it is brought to the notice of this Court that 50 per cent of the compensation has already been deposited and 8 per cent interest has been levied, which is on the higher side.
Therefore, insofar as the remaining 50 per cent of the compensation amount is concerned, the interest shall be calculated at 7.5 per cent per annum.
Miscellaneous applications, pending if any, shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICE K.SURENDER Date: 12.06.2024 NDS THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER M.A.C.M.A. No.1342 OF 2010 Date: 12.06.2024 NDS
